newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRA bombing a betrayal of peace process - Bruton.
newsitem.headline: IRA bombing a betrayal of peace process - Bruton.

text.p: The admission by the Provisional IRA that they had bombed the British Army headquarters in Lisburn "was a cynical betrayal of the peace process", Irish prime minister John Bruton told parliament on Wednesday.

"This betrayal came from an organisation that told politicians that their original ceasefire would hold in all circumstances. Now it seems that the IRA intend to continue to maintain the option of violence to be used as and when it is deemed to be politically useful," he said.
Bruton said Ireland could not be hostage to political manoeuverings by a violent movement that was only willing to give up violence if it got the terms it dictates to everybody else.
"The strategy of the ballot box in the one hand and the gun in the other was, after all, first originated by the Nazis," he said.
Bruton said parliament would hold a special debate on Northern Ireland on Thursday, to send out a clear message that the use of violence has no support in the Republic of Ireland.

He also said that the British and Irish governments must continue to give leadership in the peace process. They had tabled proposals to break the deadlock that was developing over the decommissioning of arms and he invited the parties at the talks to return to that proposal, so that the talks could move on to the substantive issues.
Contact with the British administration was continuing on an hourly basis, he said.
Opposition leaders also condemned the car bomb attacks which injured 20 soldiers and 11 civilians.
